audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gives Gragas six stages and Skill one, so no stage reads Kassadin - yet whys[6] ends 'this lane is finally mine', late says 'I win every clean 1v1', and the full layer's own 2+ items card says 'The monster is awake... Hunt.' while its side still reads Gragas. Two more internal disagreements sit at Level 1 and Level 3, where whys[0] says 'neither can commit' and whys[2] says 'I farm even' against a chart that hands both stages to Gragas.
audit.why: Kassadin loses this 46.67% over 30 games, so a Gragas-heavy chart is the right shape overall - but the 2+ items stage is the one place every prose source in both layers agrees Kassadin has taken over, and the chart contradicts all of them.
audit.corrected: 2+ items flipped to Kassadin in both layers. Level 1 and Level 3 left alone deliberately: the content whys call them even but the full-layer phase cards are generic boilerplate shared with other matchups, so there is no bespoke evidence to flip them on - flagged in notes instead.

audit.whatIsWrong: Body Slam is named as the matchup-defining cooldown eleven times across the two layers and its duration appears nowhere. Same for Barrel Roll, Explosive Cask and Riftwalk.
audit.why: Body Slam is 14/13.5/13/12.5/12s - a genuine 14-second window at rank 1, which is what 'punish the cooldown hard' is supposed to mean. Barrel Roll is 10/9/8/7/6s and the cask's potency INCREASES the longer it sits before detonating, so a ripening cask is a growing threat rather than a fixed one. Explosive Cask is 100/85/70s. Riftwalk is 5/3.5/2s, and the drop from 5s to 2s across its three ranks is the real reason the lane turns at two items.
audit.corrected: Body Slam's 14s added to the Lvl 2-3 spike and the cooldown block; Barrel Roll's 10s and its ripening cask, Explosive Cask's 100s and Riftwalk's 5-to-2s spread added alongside.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three problems. (1) breakdown.late says to 'Q-silence the counterplay' - Null Sphere has no silence. (2) mid says "Drunken Rage's drink heals him through what little I land" and whys[3] says "Drunken Rage's drink heals him on every engage" - Drunken Rage grants bonus magic damage on the next attack and damage reduction, it does no healing. The heal is Happy Hour, his passive, which triggers on every skill cast. (3) The decisive mechanical interaction in the lane is absent from both layers: Body Slam collides with the FIRST enemy unit it meets, so a minion between you and Gragas eats his engage outright.
audit.why: Getting the heal source wrong changes what the reader does: if the heal came from W they would try to dodge the empowered auto, when in fact Happy Hour fires off every cast including the Barrel Roll poke he throws from 850 range, which is why Grievous Wounds has to be bought rather than played around. And the first-unit collision on Body Slam is the answer to the page's own eleven-times-repeated instruction to 'respect his E timer' - you do not have to time it if you stand behind a minion.
audit.corrected: Silence removed; the heal reattributed to Happy Hour with anti-heal named; Body Slam's first-unit collision written into early, mid and the interactions block. Also added the one genuinely favourable interaction the page never claimed: Null Sphere's shield absorbs magic and Gragas is magic damage end to end, so here the shield really is armour.
sources: champ-data/_kits/gragas.json (P Happy Hour: 'periodically heals upon using a skill'; W: 'bonus magic damage... reducing damage received'; E: 'collides with the first enemy unit')

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns had no cooldown in it - just 'punish the cooldown hard' and 'read it like a second minimap'.
audit.why: Body Slam 14s at rank 1 is the punishable window; Explosive Cask is 100s at rank 1; Riftwalk answers at 5s and later 2s.
audit.corrected: Numbers written in, plus the note that a minion in the way makes the timer moot.

audit.whatIsWrong: Force Pulse is treated as unreliable everywhere (the generic phase card says 'E only charges when spells fly, so passive lanes starve your waveclear'), but nothing points out that this specific lane is the opposite case.
audit.why: Force Pulse charges from spells cast in Kassadin's vicinity. Drunken Rage is a 5-second cooldown Gragas presses constantly, and Barrel Roll is 10/9/8/7/6s on top of it, so against Gragas your E is one of the few lanes where it is reliably armed.
audit.corrected: Written into late: his cast tempo is what keeps your Force Pulse charged.
sources: champ-data/_kits/kassadin.json (E: 'draws energy from spells cast in his vicinity')

edits.before: Gragas' first power window — he E's (Body Slam) into you, drinks W for the empowered auto, and Q's (Barrel Roll) the chunk you backed into, while your only answer is a single Q shield.
edits.after: Gragas' first power window - he E's (Body Slam) into you, drinks W for the empowered auto, then Barrel Roll (Q) where you retreat. His E is 14s at rank 1 and stops on the first unit it touches.

edits.before: Gragas owns this lane the second he hits 2 — Body Slam (E) into you, drink Drunken Rage (W) for the empowered auto, then Barrel Roll (Q) the spot you retreat to as he walks off. My only defense is the Null Sphere (Q) shield, and it's on a long cooldown with a mana cost I can't afford to spam, so I throw Q purely to last-hit at max range and eat the poke. Don't try to trade his Body Slam back at level 1-3; I have no dash and no kill pressure, so respecting his E timer is the whole game. The one thing in my favor is Void Stone — his whole kit is magic damage, so I take 15% less than he expects, which is what keeps the chip survivable until 6.
edits.after: Gragas owns this lane the second he hits 2 - Body Slam (E) into you, drink Drunken Rage (W) for the empowered auto, then Barrel Roll (Q) the spot you retreat to as he walks off. Body Slam collides with the FIRST unit in its path, so keep a minion between the two of you and his 14-second engage lands on a caster instead of on you. My only other defense is the Null Sphere (Q) shield, but it absorbs magic and his whole kit is magic, so here it is real armour rather than decoration - I still throw it to last-hit at max range when he is not stepping up. Void Stone shaves 15% off everything he throws, which is what keeps the chip survivable until 6.

edits.before: Level 6 is where I stop being free. Riftwalk lets me blink the instant he commits Body Slam, so I either dodge the engage or wait for him to whiff E and punish with R-in, Q, Force Pulse. But this is still his window, not mine — he can E-Flash dive me, his W damage reduction eats my pre-item burst, and Drunken Rage's drink heals him through what little I land. I'm playing for safety and short blink-trades, not a kill. Bait the Body Slam, blink the moment his dash leaves his hands, and let the cooldown be your opening. Catalyst into Rod of Ages turns every minute survived into the HP and mana that flips this.
edits.after: Level 6 is where I stop being free. Riftwalk lets me blink the instant he commits Body Slam, so I either dodge the engage or wait out the 14 seconds and punish with R-in, Q, Force Pulse. But this is still his window - he can E-Flash dive me, his W damage reduction eats my pre-item burst, and Happy Hour heals him a little on every single cast, poke included, so buy Grievous Wounds before you plan a long trade. edits.before: This is the matchup I farmed twelve minutes of poke to reach. With Riftwalk maxed and Rabadon's/Nashor's online, I blink onto him repeatedly, his single-target Body Slam can't catch a target that's already two dashes away, and his W damage reduction doesn't survive my stacked R recasts plus Nether Blade on-hit. Void Stone keeps shrinking his magic output the whole game while my AP only grows. Don't get greedy mid-game and hand him a lead that delays this — once I'm at two items, I win every clean 1v1 and I'm the one picking when it starts.

With Riftwalk at 2s and Rabadon's/Nashor's online, I blink onto him repeatedly, his single-target Body Slam can't catch a target that's already two dashes away, and his W damage reduction doesn't survive my stacked R recasts plus Nether Blade on-hit. His cast tempo works for me now too - a 5s Drunken Rage and an 8s Barrel Roll keep Force Pulse charged, so my cone is armed in every fight. Once I'm at two items I win every clean 1v1, and I'm the one picking when it starts.

edits.after: He out-sustains and out-trades me through 4-5 - Happy Hour trickles health back on every cast he makes, so buy anti-heal and weather it, never race him.

edits.before: Track Gragas’s Body Slam: His engage and his escape in one button — punish the cooldown hard. It’s down or you don’t go.

notes: Two factual corrections. (1) breakdown.late called Null Sphere a silence; Kassadin's Q has no silence - Riot's text is damage, channel interrupt, and a shield absorbing magic damage. (2) content.mid and whys[3] both credited the healing to Drunken Rage. Drunken Rage gives bonus magic damage on the next attack plus damage reduction and heals nothing; the heal is Happy Hour, the passive, which fires on every skill cast - so it is bought against with Grievous Wounds rather than dodged. The decisive interaction missing from both layers: Body Slam collides with the FIRST enemy unit, so a minion in the path eats the engage the page tells you eleven times to respect. Also added: Null Sphere's shield is magic-absorbing and Gragas is magic damage end to end, making this one of the few lanes where the shield is real armour, and Gragas's 5s Drunken Rage keeps Force Pulse charged where most lanes starve it. LEVEL CHART: whys[0] ('neither can commit') and whys[2] ('I farm even') both describe even stages that the chart awards to Gragas; I did not flip them because the full-layer phase cards there are boilerplate shared verbatim with other Kassadin matchups, so there was no bespoke evidence either way. Only 2+ items was flipped, where all four sources agree.
